title: RAG citation source_url rendered as <a href> with no scheme validation (user-ingested URL → stored/DOM XSS on click)
taxonomy: M1 — SSRF / unsafe-scheme via stored URL field
description: A knowledge-chunk citation's source_url is rendered directly as an anchor href in the customer chat UI. source_url is a USER-ingested field: the RAG submission endpoints persist it verbatim from the request body with zero validation (browser extension: `source_url: body.url ?? null`; web-ui/ios-shortcut/batch identical), and the approve pipeline forwards it unvalidated into the ingested chunk (approve/route.ts:132 `source_url: row.source_url ?? undefined`). No scheme allow-list exists anywhere from ingest to render. A `javascript:` (or `data:`/`file:`) URL therefore reaches `<a href={c.source_url}>`; React renders javascript: hrefs (dev-only warning, still clickable), so a same-tenant user who retrieves the poisoned chunk in chat and clicks the citation executes attacker script in the app origin. This is the scan-extras 'SSRF / unsafe-scheme via stored *_url field' shape (source_url is explicitly a user-persisted-and-rendered field, NOT operator/env config, so it is not fp-rules exempt). Blast radius is intra-tenant (chunks are tenant-scoped) and gated by coordinator approval of the submission + a user click, which is why this is Medium rather than High.
evidence: MessageSources.tsx:55 {c.title} rag/submit/extension/route.ts:45 source_url: body.url ?? null, // no z.string().url(), no scheme check rag/submit/web-ui/route.ts:41 source_url: body.source_url ?? null, rag/queue/[id]/approve/route.ts:132 source_url: row.source_url ?? undefined, // forwarded unvalidated format-block.ts:142 source_url: c.source_url, // passed straight into the citation DTO
okWhen: source_url is validated to an http(s) scheme allow-list at ingest (or at render) before it is persisted/rendered, OR the citation link is stripped/disabled for non-http(s) schemes.
notOkWhen: A user-submitted source_url with a javascript:/data:/file: scheme is stored and later rendered as a clickable citation href in another user's chat session.
